div.div:
suffīmentum , i, n. suffio,
I.fumigation, incense (cf.: “odor, fragrantia): in iis sine illius suffimentis expiati sumus,” Cic. Leg. 1, 14, 40 : “quia suffimentum sit (laurus) caedis hostium et purgatio,” Plin. 15, 30, 40, § 135 ; cf. Fest. pp. 348 and 349 Müll.— Plur., Veg. Vet. 1, 19 sq.; 4, 12.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
